prompt_md: Start with a 1 m ribbon. Cut it at a uniformly random point and keep the left piece; repeat. On average, how many cuts until your piece is shorter than 1 cm?
prompt_short: Keep cutting a 1 m ribbon at random. Average cuts to get under 1 cm?
hint_md: Track the logarithm of the length.
explain_intuition_md: Each cut keeps half the ribbon on average, so counting halvings suggests 7 cuts to get from 100 cm under 1 cm. But a random cut often keeps much less than half, and repeated shrinking follows the typical factor, not the average one: in log terms each cut shrinks the ribbon by a factor of e. Shrinking by a factor of 100 then takes about 1 + ln 100, roughly 5.6 cuts.
explain_math_md: Each $-\ln U_i$ is exponential with mean 1, so the log-shrinkages form a rate-1 Poisson process. The number of cuts needed to pass $\ln 100$ is one more than a Poisson count with mean $\ln 100$: $$E[N] = 1 + \ln 100 \approx 5.61$$
